messages:
alex: noticing a weird drop in tokens/sec on the east cluster after the kernel mixpoint change. tokens/sec down ~35% on avg for 512-1024 seqs. $/M tokens spiked too.

maria: timeline? when did we flip the mixpoint?

alex: rolled the new heuristic 2am UTC yesterday. it shifts kernel choice to flashv2 for seq>=600, fused for <600.

ryan: saw the alert. dashboard shows KV hit rate dropped ~12% at the same time. could be interaction between batching and cache eviction.

sam: can you paste the perf numbers?

alex: short summary: baseline (old heur) 850 tokens/s on p3 with our model, now ~550. cost $/M went from ~$1.20 to ~$1.85 on those runs. nvprof traces attached to a ticket.

julia: i pulled a perf trace — GPU utilization dropped during small-batch tails. roofline indicates we went from compute-bound to memory-bound on the attention kernel for these shapes.

maria: that matches KV behavior — more misses => longer KV loads => microbatches with small seqs hit the wrong kernel.

infra-bot: deploy 2056700000 triggered kernel-mixpoint update by @alex at 2025-11-03T02:04:00Z :package: 

ryan: hypothesis: mixpoint threshold too aggressive, causing flip-flopping across sequential requests and hurting batching. also no hysteresis in the selector.

sam: i ran a flamegraph for the request path — lots of time in memory copies when mixpoint chooses flash for mid-length sequences.

julia: suggestion: add a KV-aware selector that factors in current kv_cache_hit_ratio and current microbatch_size distribution. simple rule: if kv_hit_ratio < 0.9 or avg_batch_size < 8, prefer fused.

alex: happy to try. quick override i used locally:
```
--kernel-mixpoint=seq512:fused,seq1024:flashv2
--kernel-hysteresis=seq:64
--selector-kv-threshold=0.88
```

maria: nice. also try increasing kv ttl for hot prefixes by 10s and see if hit rate recovers — that's low-risk.

sam: can we add a backoff so the selector doesn't change kernel per-request? like a per-worker sticky kernel for N seconds.

ryan: yes — sticky kernel per worker + hysteresis should reduce thrashing and stabilize batch patterns.

alex: i ran a quick A/B on a single host with sticky=10s + selector-kv-threshold=0.9. tokens/sec recovered to ~800, cost back near baseline. need larger run.

julia: great. we should also add metric: kernel_switch_rate per minute and correlate with tokens/sec and kv_hit_ratio.

maria: put straight into an infra experiment: 10% traffic with sticky=10s & kv_threshold=0.9, 10% with increased kv-ttl, rest baseline. capture kernel_switch_rate, avg_batch, kv_hit, tokens/s, $/M.

alex: creating experiment now and will dump results in the perf ticket. ticket: INF-4312. linking dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/dashboards/INF-4312 (brief)

infra-bot: experiment INF-4312 created by @alex. cohort sizes: 10/10/80.

sam: small ask: add a low-overhead profiler marker around kernel selection so we can see per-request reasons for choice (seq, kv_hit_ratio, batch_size).

ryan: i'll add the marker and a tiny sampling tracer. lightweight.

alex: thanks all — next update after 2h experiment run or earlier if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

maria: ack. adding a playbook entry in #eng-runtime-runbooks for rollback if cost anomaly exceeds 20% during the experiment.

julia: fyi — if experiment shows sticky works, we should consider making default selector KV-aware with hysteresis and a config flag to tune mixpoint.

alex: agreed. will collect logs and post a short postmortem if we need larger fixes.

ryan: one more thing — add an integration test that simulates kv_miss storm + mixed seq distribution; that caught regressions before.

alex: noted. will add test to perf-regressions suite.

infra-bot: experiment INF-4312 completed (2h). summary pending upload to INF-4312 ticket.
